context: Sinai endorses the Medinan-addition judgement on the basis of the credal-formula parallels (Q 2:4, 4:60.162, 5:59), but it is a text-internal stylistic argument, not a claim of textual corruption.

author: Nicolai Sinai

claim_en: Reports Nöldeke’s argument that Q 29:46 is a Medinan addition (because of the injunction to dispute with scripture-owners, which Nöldeke thinks presupposes fighting), then Sinai judges that argument hardly convincing.
context: Nöldeke (1860, 116) is cited inside the passage; Sinai rejects this first argument but later endorses the Medinan-addition judgement on other grounds (see kt-q29-1).

claim_en: Sinai argues that unless passages with a distinct stylistic and terminological profile can be compellingly placed in a late seventh-century context, the traditional dating of the standard rasm to 650 or earlier should be the default view.
context: Conclusion of Part II. The article itself calls the argument "not unassailable" (see bs2-q48-1).

author: Nicolai Sinai

claim_en: Sinai raises as an objection that there might have been more passages (such as Q 48:24, makka for bakka) corrected in the rasm, i.e. post-prophetic emendation of the consonantal text.
context: Stated as an objection to his own argument, then he defends the default dating. Q 48:24 is not claimed to be a specific alteration; the listing is of possible cases raised as objections.
